llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了临床股骨柄下沉，但未涉及生物力学建模或有限元分析。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA or biomechanical modeling of stress shielding, micromotion, or implant-bone interface mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究单锥度股骨柄下沉的特征、相关因素及后果。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析初次全髋置换术后X线片。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize subsidence of a single-taper femoral stem and identify associated factors and clinical sequelae.
summary_en.method: Retrospective radiographic review of primary total hip arthroplasty cases.
summary_en.result: Subsidence was associated with specific implant and patient factors, and correlated with adverse outcomes.
summary_en.validation: Clinical validation using serial radiographic measurements.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究全髋关节置换术中万古霉素的骨内给药，未涉及任何生物力学或植入物力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses antibiotic delivery and infection prevention in THA, with no quantification of femoral stress shielding, micromotion, or any contact mechanics/FEA modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估骨内万古霉素在全髋置换中的组织浓度和效率
summary_zh.method: 随机对照临床试验比较骨内与静脉给药
summary_zh.result: 骨内给药显著提高局部组织浓度且效率更优
summary_zh.validation: 临床人体试验数据验证

summary_en.motivation: To compare tissue concentrations and efficiency of intraosseous versus intravenous vancomycin administration in total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A randomized controlled clinical trial with tissue sampling and pharmacokinetic analysis.
summary_en.result: Intraosseous administration achieved significantly higher local tissue concentrations with improved efficiency.
summary_en.validation: Clinical human trial with direct tissue concentration measurements.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the association between acetabular bone loss severity and patient-reported outcome measures and reoperation rate in revision total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Retrospective cohort analysis of 248 revision THA cases.
summary_en.result: More severe bone loss was associated with higher reoperation rate but not with patient-reported outcomes.

papers.title: Retrospective Case-Control Study Genes Related to Bone Metabolism That Justify the Condition of Periodontal Disease and Failure of Dental Implants in Patients with down Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Down syndrome patients show success rates in dental implants much lower than those observed in the general population. This retrospective case-control study aimed to identify possible genes that are related to the regulation of inflammatory responses and bone metabolism related to periimplantitis and implant loss, as well as genes related to bone quality. This process involved using the functional analysis of the gene expression software Transcriptome Analysis Console (TAC version 4.0 Applied BiosystemsTM, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) and a search for possible candidate genes involved. The focus was placed on the 93 genes related to periodontitis, periimplantitis, bone loss, implant loss, and genes related to bone quality and regulators underlying the establishment and maintenance of osseointegration. Five genes showed statistically significant results (p < 0.05) in our comparison. Four of them, IL1B (p = 0.023), IL1RN (p = 0.048), BGLAP (p = 0.0372) and PTK2 (p = 0.0075) were down-regulated in the periodontal disease and implant rejection group, and only one was overexpressed: FOXO1A (p = 0.0552). The genes with statistically significant alterations described in this article determine that the group of Down syndrome patients with periodontal disease and implant failure is a group of patients genetically susceptible to suffering from both conditions together.

summary_zh.validation: 基于临床样本的基因表达统计分析

summary_en.motivation: To identify genetic factors underlying the high failure rate of dental implants in Down syndrome patients.
summary_en.method: A retrospective case-control study using Transcriptome Analysis Console to analyze 93 genes related to bone metabolism and inflammation.
summary_en.result: Five genes (IL1B, IL1RN, BGLAP, PTK2, FOXO1A) showed statistically significant differential expression between groups.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of gene expression data from clinical samples.
